analyst.summary: Timken India, the domestic arm of the US bearings major, makes components used across industrial machinery, automobiles and railways. FY26 revenue grew a modest 8.2% and profit grew 14%, but operating margins compressed on raw-material cost inflation and competitive pricing pressure. The company is investing in a new railway-bearing plant to capture India's freight-corridor and high-speed-rail capex cycle, and carries essentially no debt. The stock has fallen over the past one and two years even as earnings kept growing, reflecting a de-rating from a previously rich valuation -- and at nearly 48 times trailing earnings, it is still not cheap. We rate it a Hold: a high-quality, debt-free business, but priced for more growth than the current numbers or near-term guidance clearly deliver.
